text:
Do not press my hands.
The lasting time will come
to rest beneath much dust
and shadow in the woven fingers.

And you would say: “I cannot
love her, for her fingers have crumbled
like harvested sheaves.”

Do not kiss my mouth.
The moment will come, full
of fading light, when I shall have no lips
upon the damp earth.

And you would say: “I loved her, but I cannot
love her now, when she no longer breathes
the broom's scent from my kiss.”

I would be anguished to hear you,
and you would speak, mad and blind,
while my hand lies on your brow
when my fingers break,
and my breath descends upon your face
full of longing.

So do not touch me. I would lie
if I said I gave you my love
in these outstretched arms,
in my mouth, my neck;
and you, believing you drank it all,
would deceive yourself like a blind child.

For my love is not only this sheaf,
reluctant and weary, of my body,
that trembles at the touch of haircloth
and lags behind me in every flight.

It is what lies in the kiss, not the lip;
what breaks the voice, not the breast: it is
God's wind, passing through me, cleaving
the branch of my flesh, a wanderer!

translation.title: Do not press my hands...
